subject: Intermittent TCP truncation on private link — path MTU and SG rule audit
body:
From: Chris Dunn <chris.dunn@acme-logistics.com>
To: naomi_feldman, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: netops@acme-logistics.com
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent TCP truncation seen during private cutover

Hi Naomi / Neha,

We started the private cutover to Redwood Private yesterday evening. Since then we're seeing intermittent TCP connections that appear to 'truncate' — large payloads (file uploads, some RPC responses) fail with RST/ICMP frag-needed traces on our edge. Short transfers are fine. Attached is a packet capture and our SG dump. Can you advise? This is impacting a set of batch jobs.

Thanks,
Chris
---

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Chris Dunn <chris.dunn@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor, marcus_lin, karthik_iyer, netops@acme-logistics.com
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 11:04:31 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent TCP truncation seen during private cutover

Thanks Chris — I've pulled the pcap and SG dump. Initial read: we see repeated ICMP "fragmentation needed" with DF set on the server->client path, and packets being retransmitted then reset. Short flows are OK (fit under MTU), large flows hit the DF and fail.

Quick triage steps I'm requesting from your side before we dig deeper:
- Run traceroute --mtu from the Acme edge toward the Redwood VPC IP and capture the hops (helps confirm where PMTU is dropping).
- Confirm whether any transit device (customer firewall or branch gateways) is doing MSS clamping or explicitly setting DF.
- On your side, temporarily lower server MSS with iptables clamp as a test: iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu

I'm looping Marcus and Karthik to verify the Redwood edge config and SG processing. Attaching the pcap we pulled and our PMTU playbook for reference.

-N

> > We started the private cutover to Redwood Private yesterday evening...

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Chris Dunn <chris.dunn@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: marcus_lin, karthik_iyer, netops@acme-logistics.com
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 13:20:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TCP truncation seen during private cutover

Thanks Chris / Naomi — looked through the capture. Notes: 
- Packet shows IP DF=1 and ICMP type 3 code 4 (frag needed) coming from a transit hop two hops before the Redwood front-door. Hops are asymmetric: the forward path uses a different egress than the return.
- Acme firewall is performing deep packet inspection (DPI) and has an MTU rewrite policy on the forward chain; DPI is known to drop fragments in our infra if reassembly state doesn't match.
- Security group config from the dump looks fine (no explicit size limits) but the inspection appliance is not an SG — it's an inline device at Acme.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Enable MSS clamping at Acme firewall or at the source host as Naomi suggested. That will avoid DF-triggered ICMP and fragmentation.
2) If clamping can't be applied quickly, we can temporarily accept fragment reassembly at the Redwood front-door by setting the firewall path to allow fragmented packets from Acme ASN range, but that has DPI/IDS implications.
3) As a diagnostic, run: tracepath <redwood-vip> from the edge host (shows MTU at each hop) and tcpdump on the egress facing the firewall to capture DF packets and the ICMP responses.

I've opened NETOPS-4821 to track. Marcus — can you confirm whether our edge is currently configured to drop fragments or if there's any MTU rewriting in the edge pipeline?

-Neha

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Chris Dunn <chris.dunn@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer, netops@acme-logistics.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TCP truncation seen during private cutover

Quick update from the Redwood edge side:
- We do not rewrite MTU on egress; our front-door accepts fragments but we drop fragments that arrive with inconsistent conntrack state in the edge NAT path. The conntrack window is tight for high-concurrency flows; when Acme's DPI rewrites packets the hash changes and we sometimes see conntrack misses leading to resets.
- We can temporarily relax conntrack helper timing for Acme tenant (NETOPS-4821) for the cutover window. Long-term we prefer MSS clamping upstream.

Action plan:
- Acme to run tracepath/tcpdump and apply MSS clamp on the firewall or source host today (Chris).
- Redwood to relax conntrack short-term + add an explicit PMTU monitoring alert to the console for the Acme private route.
- We'll coordinate a postmortem with packet captures and decision log after the cutover.

Marcus

Cc: netops@acme-logistics.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent TCP truncation seen during private cutover

Thanks all — summarizing next steps so everyone has the single source of truth: 
1) Chris / Acme netops: run tracepath --mtu and tcpdump on your egress; apply the IPTABLES TCPMSS clamp rule or edge firewall MSS clamp. Confirm by 18:00 PT today. (Chris)
2) Marcus: apply the temporary conntrack relax for Acme tenant (NETOPS-4821) and enable PMTU monitoring alerting tied to the Acme route.
3) Neha & Naomi: once MSS clamp is in place, we'll retest uploads and gather a 30-minute capture to validate. If uploads still fail, we'll perform a side-by-side path capture to examine ECMP differences.

I'll keep the ticket updated and schedule a 30-min bridge if we don't see improvement. Thanks for the quick coordination — this workflow will be useful as we onboard other private customers with DPI appliances.

- Naomi

Attachments referenced: acme_edge-trace-20260517.pcap, acme_sg_dump-20260517.txt, redwood-playbook-pmtu-check.pdf
